summary.text: Natalie Ziegler is a Democratic member of the Maryland House of Delegates from District 9A who has served since January 2023 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
A former CNN researcher and producer who owns Carroll Mill Farm in Howard County, she chairs the House Environment and Transportation Committee's Agriculture and Aquaculture Subcommittee.

paragraphs.text: Ziegler was born in New York City in 1955, graduated from Abbot Academy in 1972, and earned a bachelor's degree in psychology with high honors from Oberlin College in 1977 and a master's degree in economics and foreign policy from the Johns Hopkins University School of Advanced International Studies in 1986.
She worked at CNN as a senior researcher and segment producer from 1986 to 1994 and was a producer at the Forum Network from 1999 to 2000.
From 2001 to 2022 she was co-owner and managing partner of Commonwealth Imports, LLC, which operated as Natalie Ziegler Designs, and she has owned Carroll Mill Farm in Howard County since 1990.

Ziegler served on the Howard Community College Board of Trustees in 2020 and 2021 and has been a court-appointed special advocate with Voice for Children and a literacy tutor at the South Baltimore Learning Center.
She was elected to the House in November 2022 and took office on January 11, 2023.
She serves on the Environment and Transportation Committee, chairs its Agriculture and Aquaculture Subcommittee, co-chairs the House Rural Caucus, and chairs the Howard County House Delegation.
Since 2024 she has served on the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Environmental Trust.
